plan.hypothesis: Choosing, for every plain SwinIR pixel, the corner of its enclosing 8-bit RGB lattice cell whose BT.601 luminance is closest to the continuous prediction will improve frozen Urban100-12 mean paired PSNR-Y by at least 0.05 dB versus the fixed two-pass horizontal-flip reference while keeping latency at or below 2.5 times the reference.
plan.mechanism: Independent per-channel rounding need not be the enclosing RGB lattice corner that best preserves the continuous model's luminance. The candidate evaluates all eight floor/ceiling corners and deterministically selects the one minimizing absolute BT.601-luminance displacement, with RGB squared displacement as a tie-break. My inference is that if the float prediction is locally informative about target luminance, reducing output-quantization displacement can preserve that information. The method does not estimate or feed back an LR residual and does not spatially filter or rescale the prediction.
plan.baseline: Comparator is the existing fixed two-pass SwinIR-S x2 horizontal-flip ensemble reference. The distinct candidate path uses exactly one plain, unensembled SwinIR-S x2 prediction followed only by per-pixel RGB lattice selection before the trusted adapter's output handling.
plan.why_not_g1_retry: This performs no prediction ensemble, transform, or extra model forward, so it does not retry G1. It does not form an LR-versus-SR residual or backproject, unlike G2; attenuate or amplify spatial frequency content, unlike the forbidden G3 shrinkage family; expand, reverse, or locally adapt luminance contrast, unlike G4; compress chroma to enforce an RGB gamut boundary; estimate or remove phase-locked 2x2 bias; or retune/add complexity to any stopped route. It instead changes the discrete RGB lattice representative of each continuous plain-model pixel to minimize luminance quantization displacement.

new_evidence.claim: Mei et al. formulate digital pixel values as discrete and report that incorporating a soft-rounding intensity prior can improve PSNR/SSIM in restoration, including an experiment on natural images; they also warn that naive post-rounding can harm restored structure.
new_evidence.why_distinct: This motivates treating output discretization explicitly. The paper does not test SwinIR or the proposed RGB-corner rule; applying its quantization insight to luminance-preserving lattice selection is my inference, and involves no stopped spatial or ensemble mechanism.

new_evidence.claim: Li et al. report that quantization range handling materially affects SR reconstruction quality and that their trained PAMS quantization scheme can retain competitive PSNR in quantized SR networks.
new_evidence.why_distinct: Their work concerns trained weight/activation quantization, not output postprocessing, so it supplies only primary evidence that SR is quantization-sensitive. My candidate is a training-free output lattice choice and does not reuse a stopped route.

controls: Twelve Urban100 x2 pairs selected by fixed study-id/filename hash excluding historical and local reserved IDs, before search; no image or score selection
Candidate: plain fixed SwinIR-S x2 prediction followed by one agent-authored deterministic array function
Comparator: existing fixed two-pass horizontal-flip SwinIR-S x2 reference; no optimization or reopening G1
CPU float32, four reference threads, same weights, official padding, RGB/uint8 conversion, Y metric, border crop 2
No training, extra weights, model forwards in candidate code, parameter sweeps, repeated holdout access, or automatic retries
All constants frozen in candidate.py and research.json before registration; synthetic checks only before registration
plan.stop_route: A valid negative eliminates fixed per-pixel selection among the eight enclosing 8-bit RGB lattice corners by minimum BT.601-luminance displacement, with RGB-distance tie-breaking; it does not justify retuning weights, enlarging the lattice neighborhood, or adding adaptive complexity.

parameters.input_clamp: clip each plain float RGB component to [0,1]
parameters.candidate_set: all eight Cartesian floor/ceiling corners of the enclosing RGB lattice cell
parameters.primary_selection: minimum absolute luminance displacement using fixed BT.601 weights R=0.299, G=0.587, B=0.114
parameters.tie_break: minimum squared RGB displacement; remaining exact ties retain fixed mask enumeration order 0 through 7
parameters.rationale: BT.601 matches the stated Y-channel evaluation convention; floor/ceiling corners are the nearest enclosing representable choices and eight-way enumeration is deterministic and inexpensive.
